description.overall: A DTU rig capture of two upside-down striped glazed cups on a white table, 10 frames in two clusters: four top-down views of the cup bases ([0]-[3]) on a fully blown white table, and six low side views ([4]-[9]) against a black curtain. The jump between [3] and [4] is a large viewpoint change (top to side) with a big exposure change, so the two clusters may connect only weakly or not at all. Texture is scarce: background is clipped white or crushed black, the cups are rotationally symmetric bands (matches slide along stripes) and the two cups are near twins, so cross-cup confusion is possible. Printed labels on bases and the stained sticker are the most distinctive features. Glossy glaze carries coherent reflections of the rig on the cup sides in [6]. Rig machinery visible at left of [6] is static background. Expect a fragmented view graph; detector-free or learned matching and exhaustive pairing look necessary.
description.subject: Two upside-down glazed cups side by side on a white table; [0]-[3] look down from above onto their bases against a blown white tabletop, [4]-[9] look from the side at low elevation against a black backdrop, with the cups filling the lower half and cut off at the bottom edge.
description.empty_regions: [0]-[3]: the white table fills most of the frame and is clipped at 255 (backdrop, unwanted, destroyed). [4]-[9]: black curtain fills the upper half, near-black/crushed (backdrop, unwanted); the white table strip is clipped. The cup bases are wanted, white and flat but mostly not clipped except at highlights; printed IKEA label and a stained sticker give the only texture there.
description.hazard_notes: Glossy glaze on both cups. In [6] at full resolution the cup sides carry legible grey X-shaped reflections/shadows of the rig structure crossing the stripes, and a specular glint on the rim; these move with the camera, not the surface. Graded coherent from [6]; other side-view cells [4],[5],[7] show similar marks on the thumbnail only.
description.third_frame: [6] - lowest sharpness of cells 1-8 and highest shadow clipping; also the only cell showing the rig machinery at left
description.notes: Full-res [0] confirms the table is blown to white; [9] shows the black backdrop is essentially uniform with a couple of specks.
description.repetition_texture: Horizontal coloured bands (yellow-green, green, blue, thin blue lines) repeat around every cup and down its height; along a band the pattern is rotationally uniform, so points slide along the stripe.
description.repetition_objects: Two near-identical cups with the same band sequence and the same IKEA base stamp, distinguishable only by the stained sticker on the right cup's base and by which side they stand on.

diagnostics.message: A reflective surface carrying a legible image was reported (on_subject). Glossy glaze on both cups. In [6] at full resolution the cup sides carry legible grey X-shaped reflections/shadows of the rig structure crossing the stripes, and a specular glint on the rim; these move with the camera, not the surface. Graded coherent from [6]; other side-view cells [4],[5],[7] show similar marks on the thumbnail only.
suggested_actions: A coherent reflection is a correspondence to a virtual point BEHIND the surface. Bundle adjustment will not remove it: measured, the flagged region's error ratio was unchanged either side of a global solve.

BUT REPROJECTION ERROR IS NOT BLIND TO IT, and an earlier version of this action said it was. Point by point a virtual point does reproject well. As a POPULATION it does not -- measured at 3.1x the mean error of the rest of the model. Several readers stopped looking because this action told them not to.
So the cheap probe is worth taking: read p95_reprojection_error beside mean_reprojection_error on the finished model, and compare error DISTRIBUTIONS over the flagged region, never individual points.
It is ON the subject, so the phantom structure lands on the surface being reconstructed.
Those features are self-consistent, so they can be RANSAC inliers. A healthy inlier_ratio is not evidence against this, and neither is a healthy MEAN.

diagnostics.message: The main subject (two inverted striped ceramic cups) is cropped rather than fully in view.
suggested_actions: Judge downstream coverage against what is VISIBLE, not against the object.
`cropped` is a framing limit of the capture; `occluded` means holes where something else is in the way. Neither is a pipeline fault.
A low point count on the missing part is expected, not a failure to fix.

RAFT flow over 9 pairs at stride 1, 640px. Motion: overall 0.1201, tail 0.1256, variability 0.0391; low-baseline risk 0%. Rotation: median 6.9 deg, 11% past 20 deg. Degeneracy: planar on 0% of pairs, pure-rotation on 0%.

diagnostics.message: 72% of the median frame is below the texture floor; corner density 460/MP.
suggested_actions: Watch spatial_coverage on features/v1, not keypoint count -- but read empty_regions FIRST and subtract. The grid's denominator is the whole frame, so where the untextured part is destroyed detail rather than merely flat, no detector can occupy those cells and one that reports occupying them is detecting on nothing.
That makes the raw ratio NOT comparable between two detectors on this capture: the one that spreads evenly across the frame wins a metric it should lose. Check where the winner's keypoints landed.
A detector-free matcher does not need a keypoint to exist first.

diagnostics.message: Filenames do not form a capture sequence.
suggested_actions: Sequential pairing is not valid; use exhaustive or retrieval pairing.
A video-trained tracker takes image order as real input; prefer one that does not.

diagnostics.message: No EXIF timestamps read; capture_interval_s and focal_35mm omitted. source_dir was not supplied.
suggested_actions: Expected when the scene applied a resize policy, which re-encodes and drops EXIF.
Pass source_dir pointing at the original images to recover it.

analysis.notes: Triage over 10 images (9 pairs, consecutive). Photometric: combined 0.105 (illumination 0.163, colour 0.080, exposure 0.079). Texture: 460 corners/MP, 72% textureless, repetitiveness 0.76. Sharpness ratio 0.76 against a median of 357. Clipping: 33.54% highlight, 1.62% shadow in the median frame. UNORDERED capture.

modules.name: FeatureDetectionSIFT
modules.summary: SIFT keypoints and RootSIFT descriptors. Classical, deterministic, CPU-only, and strong on well-lit high-texture scenes.

modules.name: SceneDescription
modules.summary: Renders a browsable contact sheet from the scene, then records what a viewer reports after looking at it. The only module whose output comes from outside the container.

modules.name: SceneMotion
modules.summary: Dense optical flow between image pairs, summarised into camera-motion scores and the two classic degeneracy tests -- planar dominance and pure rotation. GPU required.
